chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: Dick Gibson loses money on the band
summary: Gibson spent heavily and lost money; Bart Hickok bought him out.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well, did Dick Gibson book this? He booked the tour for the World's Greatest or was it booked through an office or something?
Well, yes, he did the booking at the time through an office. He got them to book the band.
Yeah. Well, he put the money up for the band, huh?
Yes.
And then did they split? Was that cooperative in some way?
Dick lost a lot of money on that band.
Oh, really?
He really did. He lost his shirt on that band.
Did he?
Yes.
Is that right?
And he was trying to do so much for it. He was doing everything he could for the band, really.
Is that right?
And he wasn't getting the right bookings and things like that.
But he wasn't experienced.

Well, no, he was putting a little bit too much money at the time, trying to make the band go over. You spend money to make money, true enough. But he was spending a little bit too much on it. At least, I think so.
Yeah.
And -- but he tried to make the band go.
What happened in the end to that?
Well, another guy took over. Bark Hickok, he bought Dick out, see.
Oh, I see.
And so he's still managing the band now. Bart.
Oh, he does?
Yes. Dick has nothing to do with the band.
Oh, I see. That one thing.
So, --
But does he see the guys still?
Oh, he had the guys at the party, and a lot of time they don't come to the party because they have other gigs.
Yeah.
So --
But they're welcome, they're always
welcome.
Yeah, whenever they can get off, something like that.
Yeah.
And I try to make all the parties he gives.
Yeah.
Which when I was with the World's Greatest Jazz Band, I missed about three of the parties.
Because you were booked somewhere else.
With the Jazz Band, and they wouldn't make it.
Yeah.
They were angry with Dick about something, you know, and that's the way it was.
Yeah.
